notes: The drummer behind the bro-country groove and its most public teacher, placed in PRODUCERS by the research as an instrumental-grammar entry. His framing is the parameter: "a small set of foundational 'money beats' (straight 2&4 radio patterns) that a player must 'solidify … then add colours and character to fit the situation,' alongside the train beat and cross-stick as the other two named country grooves. In engine terms: **one canonical pattern per tempo band, then per-song ornament (ghost notes, open-hat accents, rim clicks) layered on rather than pattern substitution.**" So this model pairs a fixed, narrow kick pattern with a rich ornament layer — ghost notes, a real open-hat probability and a rim lane — and the lowest `switchUpProb` in this section, because his stated payoff is about consistency: "model very low pattern variance within a section and change only at section boundaries." The bro-country variant he is identified with is quoted: "kick on 1 and the 'and-of-2,' heavy backbeat, 8ths in verse to 16ths in chorus, half-time chorus lifts, hard full-band drop-outs." The band is documented as "notated 78–95 with the backbeat on 2&4" — the folded reading, per the section convention. One further fact reaches the grid directly: "his records place a programmed clap and a sampled sub-kick *under* his acoustic kit, so the live and programmed layers must be written to the same grid," which is the clap layer at a very tight offset. ⚠ The entry states "Melody/chords: n/a," so **the melody, countermelody, chords and bassline numbers here are INFERRED** — a reading of the bro-country records he plays on rather than a researched fact. ⚠ Confidence is medium (research: medium-high) — "the named-groove taxonomy is documented; the notation itself is in images/video rather than text, so the exact placements are read off the records [LOW-CONF]."
